original_text: –Experimental Design–Good design is important to ensure that results observed are a result of experimental procedure–Experimental Variable–A factor in an experiment that is changed–Control–Unchanging factors in an experiment–Test group and control group–Test groups exposed to experimental variable while control group is not. –If results show no difference between control and test groups, hypothesis not supported–If results show difference in relation to predictions, hypothesis supported–If results show difference not in relation to prediction, different hypothesis needed or experiment needs better controls
explanation: This slide covers key components of experimental design. Good experimental design ensures that observations are actually caused by the experimental procedure. An experimental variable is the factor in an experiment that is intentionally changed. Controls are the unchanging factors. An experiment typically divides subjects into a test group (exposed to the experimental variable) and a control group (not exposed to it). If the outcomes show no difference between the test and control groups, the hypothesis is not supported. If there is a difference that matches the prediction, the hypothesis is supported. If a difference occurs but does not match the prediction, scientists must formulate a new hypothesis or improve experimental controls.
